title: Practice Pack: Matter in Our Surroundings
subject: Science
chapter: Topic-based: use with whichever Class 9 book your students follow
instructions: Level 1 checks the ideas, Level 2 is board-style questions, and Level 3 is Foundation-level challenge.

questions.q: Give two characteristics of the particles of matter.
questions.answer: (Any two) Particles of matter have spaces between them, are continuously moving, and attract each other.

questions.q: Define melting point and boiling point.
questions.answer: Melting point: the temperature at which a solid melts into a liquid at atmospheric pressure (ice: 273 K). Boiling point: the temperature at which a liquid starts boiling at atmospheric pressure (water: 373 K).

questions.q: What is sublimation? Give one example.
questions.answer: The change of a solid directly into a gas without becoming a liquid (and back). Examples: camphor, naphthalene, ammonium chloride.

questions.q: What is latent heat of vaporisation?
questions.answer: The heat energy needed to change 1 kg of a liquid into gas at atmospheric pressure at its boiling point, without any rise in temperature.

questions.q: Convert to the Celsius scale: (a) 300 K (b) 573 K. Convert to the Kelvin scale: (c) 25 °C (d) 373 °C.
Why does evaporation cause cooling? Give one everyday example.
questions.answer: During evaporation, the particles of the liquid take energy from the surroundings (or from the surface they are on) to change into vapour, so the surroundings cool down. Examples: we feel cool when sweat evaporates; water in an earthen pot (matka) stays cool.

questions.q: Give four factors that affect the rate of evaporation.
questions.answer: (1) Surface area: more area, faster evaporation. (2) Temperature: higher temperature, faster. (3) Humidity: more humidity, slower. (4) Wind speed: more wind, faster.

questions.q: Why do we wear cotton clothes in summer?
questions.answer: Cotton absorbs sweat well and lets it evaporate. Evaporation takes heat from the body and keeps us cool.

questions.q: Why does a gas fill the whole container it is kept in?
questions.answer: Gas particles have very weak forces of attraction and move very fast in all directions, so they spread out to fill all the available space.

questions.q: Why does steam cause more severe burns than boiling water at the same temperature?
questions.answer: Steam at 373 K carries extra energy (the latent heat of vaporisation) compared with water at 373 K. When it condenses on the skin, it releases this extra heat as well.

questions.q: Why does a desert cooler cool better on a hot, dry day than on a humid day?
questions.answer: A cooler works by evaporating water. On a dry day the air has little water vapour, so water evaporates quickly and takes away more heat. On a humid day the air already holds a lot of water vapour, so evaporation, and therefore cooling, is slower.

questions.q: Water droplets appear on the outside of a glass holding ice-cold water. Where do they come from?
questions.answer: Water vapour in the air touches the cold surface of the glass, loses energy, and condenses into liquid droplets. The water does not come through the glass.

questions.q: Arrange in increasing order of the forces of attraction between particles: water, sugar, oxygen. Explain.
questions.answer: Oxygen (gas) < water (liquid) < sugar (solid). Particles in solids attract each other most strongly, liquids less, and gases the least.

closing: Evaporation = cooling. Look for examples at home today!
